newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Sporitelna raises deposit rates.
newsitem.headline: Czech Sporitelna raises deposit rates.

text.p: The largest Czech savings bank, Ceska Sporitelna a.s. said on Friday it would raise its deposit rates for clients by 60 basis points from May 1, in response to the central bank's lowering of minimum reserve requirements.

In a statement, bank spokesman Pavel Jirousek said the move by the central bank on Thursday to reduce minimum reserve requirements to 9.5 percent from 11.5 percent beginning on May 8, would free up about 5.5 billion crowns in Sporitelna's funds.
"Ceska Sporitelna, as a manager of the largest volume of deposits among Czech banking institutions, unambiguously welcomes the decision of the (central bank)...," he said.

"On the basis of the first analysis, the board of directors expects that it will be possible to raise (deposit rates according to maturity) by as much as 0.6 percent per annum, and support the interest of citizens in increasing their savings."
It added that the board's analysis was approved as the bank's policy.
Other banks have suggested since Thursday's central bank decision that they too may raise their deposit rates.

The CNB raised its key interest rates and raised the minimum reserve requirements to 11.5 percent from 8.5 percent last June, to stifle domestic demand which had been keeping inflation stubbornly high.
But with economic growth slowing and inflation more under control, the central bank has come under heavy government pressure to loosen monetary policy.
The central bank said it took the move to lower mandatory reserves in order to encourage commercial banks to raise their deposit rates and thus more savings by citizens.
